About Us

For more than 140 years, The University of Texas System has improved the lives of Texans — and people all over the world — through education, health care, and research. The System consists of nine academic institutions, four health institutions, and The University of Texas System Administration. The institutions of the UT System employ more than 160,000 faculty, health care professionals, researchers, support staff, and student workers.

The UT System Administration is primarily based in Austin, Texas. It supports the missions of the System’s thirteen institutions by providing financial, legal, planning, purchasing, government relations, communications, development, and other central services. Serving a growing state, the UT System Administration strives to provide a welcoming, supportive work environment that embraces different perspectives - not only because it enables the organization to be stronger, creative, and thoughtful, but because it is the right thing to do. To that end, UT System Administration embraces state laws on military and former foster children employment preferences.

Purpose of Position

The purpose of the Public Safety Officer at the UT System is to help safeguard property and maintain a secure, orderly environment under the control and jurisdiction of the University of Texas System Administration. This role is responsible for enforcing rules and regulations, monitoring building access, and providing courteous service and information to employees, visitors, and contractors.

Public Safety Guards play a key role in ensuring compliance with parking regulations on UT System-controlled property, issuing permits or citations as needed. They serve as the first point of contact at building entrances, issue visitor credentials, and identify potential safety or security concerns. Through vigilance, professionalism, and a commitment to service, Public Safety Guards support the overall safety and operational integrity of the UT System.

Essential Functions

Access Control & Identification

  • Ensure all personnel entering the UT System Complex or affiliated campuses are properly identified.
  • Issue visitor badges and maintain accurate logs of all issued credentials.
  • Monitor building entrances and exits to prevent unauthorized access and ensure compliance with access protocols.

Building & Grounds Patrol

  • Conduct regular patrols of the building and surrounding grounds to identify and report potential safety and security hazards, including fires, water leaks, suspicious activity, and emergencies.
  • Monitor for maintenance issues and report them to Facilities Management or appropriate personnel.

Enforcement of Rules, Regulations & Parking

  • Enforce UT System Administration rules and regulations to help safeguard property and maintain order.
  • Direct the flow of traffic and parking of vehicles on UT System-controlled property.
  • Issue parking permits and citations in accordance with established policies and procedures.

Constituent Service & Public Assistance

  • Provide courteous and professional service to employees, visitors, and contractors.
  • Offer directions, general information, and assistance as needed to support a welcoming and secure environment.

Incident Response & Reporting

  • Respond to routine incidents and emergencies, coordinating with UT System Police or emergency services as appropriate.
  • Write clear and accurate reports on incidents occurring within the System Complex or campus.
  • Assist in building evacuations, emergency drills, and other safety-related operations.

Collaboration & Communication

  • Maintain effective communication with UT System Police, Facilities Management, and other departments.
  • Participate in safety briefings, training sessions, and departmental meetings to stay current on procedures and expectations.

Other Duties

  • Perform other related duties as assigned to support the safety and operational goals of the UT System Police Department.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Knowledge of basic security and safety principles, including access control, emergency response, and incident reporting.
  • Familiarity with UT System rules, regulations, and procedures (or ability to learn them quickly).
  • Awareness of building systems and the ability to recognize safety hazards such as fire risks, water leaks, or suspicious activity.
  • Strong interpersonal and constituent service skills for interacting with employees, visitors, and contractors in a professional and courteous manner.
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to write clear and accurate incident reports.
  • Basic computer skills for logging visitor information, writing reports, and using security systems.
  • Skilled in operating security-related equipment and technology used in daily operations.
  • Ability to remain alert, observant, and responsive during long periods of stationary or patrol duty.
  • Ability to exercise sound judgment and remain calm in stressful or emergency situations.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team, following established procedures and protocols.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information appropriately.
  • Physical ability to patrol buildings and grounds, stand or walk for extended periods, respond quickly to incidents.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree, OR Associate's Degree, OR HS Diploma or GED and 6 months of experience
  • Valid Texas Driver’s License with a good driving record.

This position requires the ability to maintain the security and integrity of UT System Administration and its infrastructure.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience as a Guard/Public Safety Officer with the U.T. System Administration or an institution police department.
  • CPR and First Aid certification preferred.

Working Conditions

  • Driving of UT owned vehicle required.
  • Uniforms and/or personal protection equipment (furnished).
  • May work in extreme temperatures.
  • May work in all weather conditions.
  • May work around standard office conditions.
  • Repetitive use of a keyboard at a workstation.
  • Climbing of stairs.
  • Lifting and moving objects.
  • Requires occasional evening or weekend hours

Additional Information

The retirement plan for this position is Teacher Retirement System of Texas (TRS), subject to a minimum of 20 hours per week and at least 135 days in length. Participation in TRS is mandatory.

Texas Tactical Protection Group is seeking professional and dependable Unarmed Security Officers to provide overnight security for an active construction site. Officers are responsible for protecting the property, equipment, materials, and personnel by maintaining a visible security presence, controlling access to the site, conducting routine patrols, and reporting any suspicious or unsafe activity.

The ideal candidate will demonstrate sound judgment, excellent communication skills, and the ability to remain alert throughout the entire shift.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Monitor and control access to the construction site, allowing entry only to authorized personnel.

  • Verify identification, credentials, and authorization of all visitors, contractors, and vendors as required.

  • Conduct routine and random foot and/or vehicle patrols of the property throughout the shift.

  • Deter theft, vandalism, trespassing, and unauthorized activity through a visible security presence.

  • Protect construction materials, equipment, tools, vehicles, and other company assets.

  • Observe and report suspicious activity, criminal behavior, or security concerns immediately.

  • Contact emergency services (Police, Fire Department, or EMS) when necessary and provide accurate information regarding emergencies.

  • Respond appropriately to incidents while remaining within company policies and state regulations.

  • Identify and report safety hazards, fire hazards, damaged fencing, unsecured gates, or other conditions that could present a risk to personnel or property.

  • Complete detailed, accurate, and timely incident reports, daily activity reports, and shift logs.

  • Maintain communication with supervisors and provide timely updates regarding significant events.

  • Ensure all gates, access points, and designated areas remain secure during the shift.

  • Maintain a professional appearance, demeanor, and customer service attitude while representing Texas Tactical Protection Group.

  • Follow all client post orders, company policies, and Texas Department of Public Safety regulations.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Valid Texas Security Officer License (Level II – Non-Commissioned).

  • High school diploma or GED preferred.

  • Ability to stand, walk, and patrol for extended periods.

  • Reliable transportation and punctual attendance.

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.

  • Ability to remain calm and make sound decisions during emergencies.

  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.

  • Must successfully pass any required background screening.

Physical Requirements

  • Walk and patrol uneven terrain throughout the shift.

  • Stand for extended periods.

  • Climb stairs and navigate active construction areas when necessary.

  • Work outdoors in varying weather conditions, including heat, cold, wind, and rain.

  • Lift up to 25 pounds occasionally.

Work Environment

This position is performed at an active construction site. Officers may be exposed to heavy equipment operations, dust, noise, and changing weather conditions. Situational awareness and adherence to all safety procedures are essential.

Professional Expectations

All Security Officers are expected to:

  • Arrive on time and ready for duty.

  • Wear the complete company-approved uniform.

  • Maintain a courteous, professional, and respectful attitude at all times.

  • Exercise integrity, vigilance, and sound judgment.

  • Preserve confidentiality regarding client operations and security procedures.

  • Represent Texas Tactical Protection Group with the highest standards of professionalism.

Texas Tactical Protection Group is committed to providing professional security services through integrity, accountability, and excellence.

jobs.title: 24/7 Security Officer FT
jobs.description:
Career Opportunities with Multipurpose Arena Fort Worth

Trail Drive Management Corporation Properties
Trail Drive Management Corp. (TDMC) is a not-for-profit venue management company in Fort Worth, Texas. TDMC manages all aspects of venue management, including but not limited to event booking, event management, marketing, IT, technical services, food & beverage, parking, security, housekeeping, changeover, maintenance, and more. TDMC manages several venues in Fort Worth, TX.

Job Summary
Trail Drive Management Corp (TDMC) is looking for a full-time 24/7 Security Officer. This position is responsible for incident reporting and general security operations directly associated with protecting the facility, its patrons, employees, and the interests of the organization. This includes the protection of all facility infrastructure and assets. Security officer personnel will complete required training, work varying schedules, investigate incidents, complete reports, and patrol the facility.

This position will be 100% on-site.

Essential Job Functions

Patrols the facility as directed to prevent or minimize property loss, property damage, personal injury, or situations having a negative impact on the organization.

Monitors and authorizes entrance through issuance of visitor's badge or check of credentials of employees, guests, and others to ensure the safety and security of the facility.

Unlocks and secures doors before and after events as directed.

Move barricades to secure/open specific areas in and around the facility as needed.

Operates security vehicles including golf carts for patrol and response to calls/incidents.

Conducts proper investigation and inquiries into all incidents, accidents, security issues, and situations impacting the facility or the Organization's interest, its employees, partners, and guests, to include but not limited to damage, losses, safety matters, or injury. Provides detailed reports to the Security Supervisor and Safety & Security Manager.

Ensures understanding and compliance with all guidance, instruction, policies and procedures of the organization and the proper execution of assigned duties.

Completes ongoing, in-service training for all security personnel, maintaining all certifications and required training as specified.

Ensures all shift-related issues, observations, and critical information are documented, verified, and accurately reported to the appropriate decision maker in a timely fashion.

Operates detection devices to screen individuals or packages and prevent passage of prohibited articles into restricted areas.

Responsible for monitoring security systems, work communications equipment, and reporting any issues with the facility systems during assigned shifts.

Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Must be a minimum of 18 years of age.

High School Diploma or Associate's Degree in Law Enforcement, Criminology, or a related field preferred.

Background in corporate security, loss prevention, military or law enforcement, and operating within a diverse workforce at major public venues.

A minimum of three (3) years of experience in the military, security, law enforcement, or a related field.

Possess a current Texas Driver's License

Be eligible to obtain a Texas Guard Card

Fluently bilingual English / Spanish strongly preferred.

Must show good judgment and common sense.

Follow directions and directives from supervisors.

Professional appearance, positive attitude

Ability to function well during a critical or emergency incident.

Ability to perform CPR and other first aid procedures.

Ability to work a flexible schedule including - nights, weekends, and holidays.

Able to communicate effectively with management, guests, and team members.

Ability to handle multiple tasks in a fast-paced, high-energy environment.

Working Conditions

Employees will work in an environment with fluctuating temperatures.

Employees must have the ability to lift, push, and pull up to 50 lbs.

Employees will regularly spend their shift standing/walking, traveling stairs, with limited to no sitting.

Employees may be exposed to high noise levels and/or fluctuating lights in event settings.

Employees must have the ability to reach, lift, and bend to perform job duties throughout the shift.

Employees may be exposed to hazards associated with moving vehicles and require strict adherence to safety protocols.

Employees may be exposed to hazardous chemicals, electrical shock risks, and vibrations throughout the shift.

Other Duties

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

jobs.title: Regional Loss Prevention Investigator
jobs.description:
Regional LP Investigator

About Our Company

At Lids Sports Group, we don’t just sell hats — we fuel fandom. As the largest licensed sports retailer in North America, we bring sports, fashion, and culture together in more than 1,300 stores nationwide. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, Lids delivers premium, fan-driven products and unforgettable retail experiences.

Our stores feature officially licensed headwear and apparel from collegiate and professional teams, alongside top brands like Champion, Nike, New Era, Lululemon Athletica, and Mitchell & Ness. We’re also the industry leader in on-demand customization, offering in-store embroidery that turns everyday gear into one-of-a-kind statements.

From specialty concept stores for the NBA and NHL to iconic clubhouse destinations for the Yankees and Dodgers, we create immersive retail experiences that celebrate the teams fans love. Through collaborations with brands like Marvel, Peanuts, and The Walt Disney Company, Lids continues to redefine how fans represent their teams — in style.

Position Summary

The Regional Loss Prevention Investigator (RLPI) is responsible for mitigating financial loss through comprehensive investigations, physical inventory audits, and policy compliance reviews. This role leverages advanced data analytics and surveillance technology to detect fraud, while providing essential training to field personnel to ensure strict adherence to corporate standards.

Principal Duties and Responsibilities

  • Investigations: Lead internal and external investigations into theft, fraud, and policy violations, conducting professional interviews to reach successful resolutions.
  • Compliance Auditing: Evaluate store records and operational procedures to ensure full compliance with company policies and applicable legal regulations.
  • Data Analytics: Utilize POS exception-based reporting and analytics software to identify patterns of loss and potential asset exposure.
  • Inventory Control: Execute full physical inventory audits to verify asset accountability and assess the accuracy of store accounting systems.
  • Risk Mitigation: Conduct specialized studies to identify the mechanics of fraud and develop preventative controls to safeguard company property and funds.
  • Reporting & Recommendations: Prepare detailed audit and investigative findings for Regional Directors, District Sales Managers, and HR, providing actionable recommendations for improvement.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with HR, field leadership, and law enforcement agencies to resolve complex cases and ensure organizational alignment.
  • Training & Support: Educate field personnel on loss prevention best practices, operational compliance, and corporate policy and procedures (SOPs).
  • Customer Service: Maintain a professional demeanor and provide high-level service in alignment with Lids Sports Group (LSG) standards.
  • Policy Adherence: Consistently support and model all company policies and performance guidelines.

Job Required Knowledge and Skills

  • Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in business or a related field; OR an Associate’s degree with 1+ years of relevant experience; OR an equivalent combination of education and professional experience.
  • Certification: Professional Interview & Interrogation certification (e.g., Wicklander-Zulawski) required.
  • Autonomy: Proven ability to work independently and manage a regional territory with minimal supervision.
  • Communication: Exceptional interpersonal skills with the ability to communicate professionally and effectively at all levels of the organization.
  • Technical Skills: Proficiency in computer operations, case management software, and security systems.
  • Licensing: Must possess a valid driver’s license and active auto insurance.

Physical Demands & Requirements

  • Ability to occasionally lift up to 50 pounds.
  • Ability to occasionally climb a ladder and work with hands overhead.
  • Ability to constantly stand on shift.
  • Ability to frequently walk on shift.
  • Ability to frequently hear and communicate verbally with customers, employees, and other personnel.
  • Ability to frequently visually observe the store and read written or digital information.
  • Ability to frequently operate a computer and mobile Point-of-Sale system, as well as maneuver relative software programs.
  • Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions. For inquires related to reasonable accommodations, please contact HR@Lids.com.

What We Offer

  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Retirement plan with company match
  • 100% employer-paid benefits, including short-term and long-term disability, life and AD&D insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program
  • Paid Time Off
  • Generous employee discount and exclusive perks
  • Ongoing career development and professional training, including discounted secondary education and certification reimbursement
  • A collaborative, innovative, and team-oriented work environment
  • Early Wage Access options
  • Bonus eligibility depending on position level

Work Environment

  • On the road! This role requires 100% travel.

Being legally authorized to work in the United States is a pre-condition of employment for this position. Current or future employment-based visa sponsorship is not available for this role.

jobs.description:
JOB DESCRIPTION
Job Description
Description:*Off-Duty Officer Required*
Position Summary:
The Internal Security Officer is a full-time, internal employee responsible for the close-in physical safety, secure transport, and logistical security planning for the Chief Executive Officer (CEO). Operating as a professional within our internal security department, this individual performs comprehensive threat mitigation, advanced site sweeps, and defensive driving.
This position requires strict compliance with Texas DPS Private Security Bureau regulations for a Level IV Personal Protection Officer (PPO).
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Duties include the following (other duties may be assigned):
• Provide discreet, low-profile physical security for the CEO during daily business operations, corporate board meetings, public appearances, and special events within the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex and during travel.
• Act as the primary security driver for the CEO.
Conduct daily pre-trip vehicle inspections, plan primary and secondary evacuation routes, manage real-time Dallas traffic or construction bottlenecks, and execute evasive driving maneuvers if threatened.
• Conduct "advance" security assessments of all locations the CEO intends to visit (offices, restaurants, event spaces). Coordinate with venue staff, identify emergency exits, and locate nearest medical trauma centers.
• Partner with internal corporate intelligence and cyber teams to monitor fixated threats, hostile communications, stalkers, or planned civil disruptions targeting the CEO or corporate office.
• Blend seamlessly into high-level corporate boardrooms, public forums, or casual events.
- Maintain flawless professional grooming standards and use elite communication skills to diffuse unwanted approaches or minor disturbances without drawing public attention.
• Serve as the immediate first responder to any medical crisis, administering trauma-level first aid, CPR, or AED usage until local Dallas emergency personnel arrive.
• Ability to maintain absolute mental focus and situational awareness during extended periods of standing, waiting, or tracking.
• This is an internal, full-time position that requires a high degree of scheduling flexibility.

jobs.title: Urgent Part-Time:Sortation Warehouse Associate(Chicago)
jobs.description:
Position in Chicago, IL Snapshot
  • Company: Amazon
  • Pay Rate: $19-$21/Hour (approx. $21.1k/Year)
  • Earn extra cash with a stable local employer.
  • Benefits: Flexible scheduling available.
  • This role focuses on your professional skills with a schedule that fits your life.
  • Location: Chicago, IL
  • New Opening: Part-Time Sortation Warehouse Associate
  • This Chicago-based role is an excellent opportunity for professionals skilled in customer service.
  • Our Amazon team in Chicago, IL is growing.
  • Benefit from working in Chicago, a key hub for the Logistics industry.
Mastering the Middle Mile

If the fulfillment center is the brain of the operation, the sortation center is the central nervous system. Welcome to the critical \"middle mile\" of the Amazon delivery network. As a Sortation Warehouse Associate, your primary objective is to group and route thousands of packages so they reach the correct local delivery hubs at lightning speed. For those seeking highly active, fast-paced part time warehouse jobs that offer intense teamwork and rapid physical movement, this is the ultimate environment.

The Sortation Experience

Work in a sort center is fundamentally different from a traditional fulfillment role. You are not picking individual items; you are dealing with sealed, completed packages that are moving rapidly down vast networks of conveyor belts. The atmosphere is charged, loud, and incredibly team-oriented. When the conveyor belts get heavily loaded during a \"rush,\" you will rely on your teammates to clear the lines and keep the supply chain moving seamlessly.

  • Rapid Package Routing: You will read complex digital routing labels as packages fly down the line, pulling them off the belt and sorting them into specific geographical chutes or designated postal carts.
  • Pallet Architecture: You will become a master of spatial reasoning. Sorting requires building perfectly stable, tightly packed pallets of boxes (often referred to as \"playing Tetris\" by our veteran associates), which are then heavily shrink-wrapped to prevent transit damage.
  • Fluid Loading Operations: Utilizing manual pallet jacks, you will safely transport these massive, wrapped pallets directly into the bellies of outbound 18-wheeler semi-trailers, staging them for the over-the-road drivers.

\"The sort center moves incredibly fast, but the flexibility is what keeps me here. Working part-time allows me to manage my college classes while still getting access to Amazon's incredible 401(k) matching and tuition assistance. It is the perfect balance.\"

Flexibility and Comprehensive Rewards

We understand that modern life requires flexible schedules. Sortation roles offer some of the most adaptable shifts in the logistics careers landscape, including morning, evening, and weekend-only options. Despite being part-time, eligible associates still unlock exceptional health, dental, and vision benefits, along with highly competitive shift differentials that boost your base pay when working non-traditional hours. You will need a strong commitment to workplace safety, the ability to lift up to 49 pounds, and a High School diploma or equivalent to join the team.

What You’ll Do

As a Rotating Warehouse Associate this position will require the employee to rotate between several key roles in the warehouse, including Forklift Operation, Selecting, Loading, Cycle Counting, and Quality Inspection. The ideal candidate will have a strong attention to detail and computer skills, be adaptable to different tasks, and demonstrate a high level of teamwork and communication skills. This employee must have good attendance, maintain safe work in the warehouse, operate all equipment in a safe and efficient manner following prescribed work methods, keep the warehouse clean, and comply with OSHA and SDS Standards. You must also be able to work in an atmosphere as cold as - 30 degrees.

Qualifications

  • Minimum of a 5 years of experience in a warehouse
  • Minimum of 2 years of RF scanning experience
  • Minimum of 2 years of inventory experience
  • Minimum of 1 year of Forklift experience
  • Minimum of 1 year of Dock Inspecting and Loading
  • Must be able to read and write in English

Physical Requirements: The physical requirements are that you must be able to carry, lift and/or move up to 50-60 pounds

Hourly Rate: $18-$19.00
